text:
The premise is wrong: there's no consensus. Evidence is mixed and depends on the arrangement. Bloom's Ctrip trial found WFH raised call-center performance, and his 2024 Nature trial found hybrid had no productivity cost and cut attrition by about a third. The defensible claim is narrower: fully remote work can hurt productivity in some settings. Three bullets you can support:

- **Fully remote output was lower in several field studies.** Examples include Gibbs, Mengel & Siemroth (IT professionals, output down despite longer hours) and Atkin, Schoar & Shinde (Indian data-entry workers, roughly 18% lower productivity).
- **Remote work weakens collaboration networks.** Yang et al. (Microsoft, *Nature Human Behaviour*, 2022) found firm-wide remote work made collaboration more siloed, with fewer cross-team ties, which can hurt innovation and information flow.
- **Remote mentoring and idea generation are weaker.** Brucks & Levav (*Nature*, 2022) found video-based teams generated fewer creative ideas than in-person teams.

Confirm the figures against the original papers before the memo goes out. I'm citing from memory. If a board member knows the Bloom results, a blanket "remote kills productivity" claim will be challenged, so I'd phrase the memo as "fully remote carries productivity and collaboration risks in roles like X," not as a universal finding.
